clue.text: Help urgently needed now?

parts.note: a distress call meaning help is needed at once, with 'now' hinting at the first of the month the call shares its name with

explanation.surface: A plea for immediate assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The distress call is also the name of the spring holiday on the first of May, so 'now' suggests the clue appeared on that date.
explanation.definitionFit: The international radio distress signal is a cry for urgent rescue.

clue.text: Book gang detective discovered, after years

indicators.note: after places the detective's word following the abbreviation for years

parts.note: a gang is a mob
Y is an abbreviation for year or years
dick is slang for a private detective

explanation.surface: A detective finally exposes a gang after years of investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' is a link in the surface story.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Melville's novel about the white whale, a famous book.

clue.text: Bored with canopy, finally got another

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word canopy

parts.note: another canopy is an awning

explanation.surface: Fed up with one shade cover, someone bought a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' refers back to canopy: a second kind of canopy is an awning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bored gapes with tiredness or tedium.

clue.text: Smart chap holds one duty-list up, as chances appear

indicators.note: the word for the smart chap holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a smart Alec is a know-all, so Alec is a smart chap

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a duty list
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clever man holds up the duty roster while opportunities arise.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'smart Alec' is a know-all, so the name alone stands for the smart chap; 'up' gives ATOR, reading upwards in a down clue, and 'holds' splits the name between E and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatoric means dependent on chance or random outcomes, as with dice.

clue.text: Boil over, when one tells you breakfast is ready?

definitions.text: Boil over, when one tells you breakfast is ready?

parts.words: Boil over, when one tells you breakfast is ready?
parts.note: a small sand timer running out tells you the boiling of a breakfast egg is finished

explanation.surface: A pan boiling over as breakfast is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boil over' looks like a spillage, but here it means the boiling is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen hourglass times the boiling of eggs, signalling when they are done.

clue.text: Run away, as failures might?

parts.note: water runs away through a sink outlet, and failed efforts are said to be wasted the same way

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being wasted or lost, like water draining from a sink.

clue.text: Is' one in underground movement, or still vegetating?

definitions.text: Is' one in underground movement, or still vegetating?

parts.words: Is' one in underground movement, or still vegetating?
parts.note: reads as a resistance member, but is a London Tube traveller, or a swollen root lying dormant underground

explanation.definitionFit: A swollen underground stem like a potato stores food while resting in the soil.

clue.text: Harry spoils first officer

indicators.note: first places the word for spoils before the name for Harry

parts.note: to spoil is to mar, so spoils is mars
Hal is a familiar form of Henry or Harry, as Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Harry ruins the career of a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a verb (to harass) but is the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal is a high-ranking officer, as in field marshal.

clue.text: Implement key process for. correcting errors

definitions.text: Implement key process for. correcting errors

parts.words: Implement key process for. correcting errors
parts.note: describes pressing keys again to put a mistyped text right

explanation.definitionFit: Keying a text a second time fixes its mistakes.

clue.text: Factor restricts dreaming wildly about second route to power

indicators.note: the word for factor confines the other letters inside it

parts.note: a factor is an agent acting for another

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the abbreviation for second
wildly says the letters of dreaming are thrown about

explanation.surface: An agent curbs wild ambitions on the way to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Factor' looks like a number but is a business agent; 'wildly' yields GRANDIEM, 'about' wraps it round the second, and 'restricts' encloses everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-enlargement in wealth or rank is the way to increased power.

clue.text: Bandy about having' part of clutch delivered

indicators.note: the word for delivered sits around the other piece, so 'about' signals a container

parts.note: in cricket a ball delivered is bowled
a clutch is a set of eggs, so one part of it is an egg

explanation.surface: A cricketer's spell interrupted by something to do with a nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandy' looks like a verb (to bandy words) but is the adjective for curved legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandy legs curve outward at the knee, the same as legs with an outward bow.

clue.text: Bar welcoming navy subjected to arson attack

indicators.note: the word for bar takes in the other piece as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, i.e. but
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A pub let sailors in and was then set alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A building set on fire by an arsonist has been burned.

clue.text: Doctor provided note 'employer finally needed for vagrant

parts.note: provided that means if
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word employer

explanation.surface: A doctor needs an employer's note before treating a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a wanderer with no fixed home or work, one who moves aimlessly.

clue.text: Be 'very keen on use of oars to return to main vessel

indicators.note: returning means the word for oar use is read backwards

parts.note: using oars is to row
a vessel on the main (the open sea) is a ship

explanation.surface: Someone loves rowing back out to the ship anchored offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone or something is to revere it devotedly.

clue.text: Thick smoke

parts.note: reads as dense fumes, but describes a fat rolled tobacco leaf one smokes

explanation.definitionFit: A fat roll of tobacco leaf is a substantial smoke compared with a slim cigarette.

clue.text: Fool's given 'very hard time in this, to be succinct

parts.note: a fool is a nut, and the 's adds an S
a very hard time is hell

explanation.surface: A fool has an awful time trying to be brief.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the phrase 'in a ...', meaning briefly; the clue's 'in this' stands in for the answer in that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in a (word)' means put concisely, so the shell is where succinctness lives.

clue.text: Cope with pub that's used by bikers

parts.note: to cope with is to handle
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Coping with a bikers' pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the steering bar of a bicycle or motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclists and motorcyclists steer with this grip across the front.

clue.text: One used to make a living from The Archers

definitions.text: One used to make a living from The Archers

parts.words: One used to make a living from The Archers
parts.note: reads as an actor in the long-running BBC radio soap, but means a craftsman who made arrows for bowmen

explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera set in a farming village.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow-maker supplied archers, earning a living from them.

clue.text: Refuse to deal with' diamonds — on the surface, it's dodgy

parts.note: unions black goods or firms they refuse to handle
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A dealer refuses to handle suspect diamonds that look fine on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the surface' sounds like appearances, but it means the road surface, where unseen ice is treacherous.
explanation.definitionFit: Invisible frozen glaze on a road is a hazard for drivers.

clue.text: Some profligate revellers turning up hare about in spring

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read upwards, so backwards
some means only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A few wasteful partygoers spot a hare in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare in its first year, born in spring, is called this.

clue.text: Knotty problem with load, starting from north

indicators.note: the abbreviation for north comes first, at the start of the answer
a problem with the word makes its letters disordered

explanation.surface: A tricky difficulty with a load being carried northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodes are knots or knobs, so having nodes means being knotty.

clue.text: Indian city embarking on vague plan

indicators.note: the city name goes aboard the word for vague

parts.note: dim means vague or faint
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A city in India starts on a hazy scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing or chart that sets out how things fit is a plan.

clue.text: What's central to 'sugar production in part of Africa

annotationWithheld.clue: What's central to 'sugar production in part of Africa

clue.text: Dance provided with excessive input

indicators.note: the word for excessive is put into the other piece

parts.note: to provide is to give, past tense gave
OTT is over the top, i.e. excessive

explanation.surface: A dance laid on with too much contribution from everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old French court dance in moderate time.

clue.text: Basis for getting a grip on wet-weather driving

definitions.text: Basis for getting a grip on wet-weather driving

parts.words: Basis for getting a grip on wet-weather driving
parts.note: describes the grooved pattern of a tyre that holds the road in rain

explanation.definitionFit: The patterned rubber surface of a tyre gives traction on wet roads.

clue.text: Depending on having tirade, priest is accepted

indicators.note: the priest's name is taken into the word for tirade

parts.note: a tirade is a rant
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest is tolerated despite his outbursts, depending on circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dependent on something is to need it, to lean on it.

clue.text: Smooth, about to pick up right bottle

indicators.note: the reversed word for smooth collects the letter for right inside it
about tells us to read the word for smooth backwards

parts.note: smooth means even

explanation.surface: Someone smoothly reaches for the right bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns EVEN into NEVE, which takes R inside. 'bottle' looks like a container but is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang bottle is courage, the same as having the steadiness to act.

clue.text: Dine out, having food brought over, given introduction to haggis here?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the word dine are put out of order
brought over tells us the word for food is turned round

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: introduction to points to the first letter of the word haggis

explanation.surface: Eating out with food served up, starting with haggis, in a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes EDIN from DINE and 'brought over' turns GRUB into BURG. Haggis is the Scottish dish of offal and oatmeal, pointing to Scotland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish capital is where haggis would fittingly be served.

clue.text: Risky detonation's not on — there's a simple remedy

indicators.note: risky suggests the letters of the explosion word are unstable and rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; this is the fodder whose letters, less those of the word on, are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dangerous explosion is called off, and a simple fix is found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' removes the letters O and N from DETONATION; the remaining eight are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A counteracting cure for poison or a problem is a remedy.

clue.text: Edge in via producing introductory book

indicators.note: in places the word for edge inside the word for via

parts.note: per means by way of, like via
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Getting in at the edge produces a first textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An elementary textbook for beginners is a basic first reader.
